html:
Zouk is a fast dance music created in Guadeloupe and Martinique around 1980, above all by the band Kassav'. The word means party in the local Creole.

Kassav' mixed the island drum traditions of gwo ka and bele with Haitian compas and modern electronic sound. Their hit Zouk-la se sel medikaman nou ni (1984) spread the style far beyond the islands.

Zouk became hugely popular in French speaking Africa, in Cape Verde and Angola, where it shaped kizomba, and in Brazil, where it gave its name to a dance. It gave the French Caribbean a confident pop voice in Creole, as reggae did for Jamaica.
